name: Pediatric lateral approach to the distal fibula
corridor: Longitudinal exposure at posterior fibular border through the interval between peroneus tertius anteriorly and peroneus longus/brevis posteriorly

positioning.text: Position supine with a bump to rotate the fibula upward or lateral as needed, keeping AP, lateral, mortise, and oblique imaging available.

setup.text: Define the physis, fragment extent, implant position, and superficial-peroneal and sural-nerve danger zones before incision.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark fibular shaft and tip, distal-fibular physis, anterior and posterior fibular borders, superficial-peroneal-nerve course, and Achilles tendon.

incision.text: Use a longitudinal incision centered on fracture and biased to posterior fibular border so a lateral plate is not directly beneath the wound.

superficial_interval.text: Raise full-thickness flaps; identify superficial peroneal nerve with proximal/anterior extension and protect short saphenous vein and sural nerve posteriorly.

deep_interval.text: Develop the plane between peroneus tertius anteriorly and peroneus longus/brevis posteriorly, limiting periosteal elevation to the fracture and implant footprint.

layers.text: Skin, sensory-neurovascular plane, peroneal fascia, peroneus-tertius/peroneal interval, limited periosteum, then fibula.

structures_encountered.text: Superficial peroneal nerve, sural nerve, short saphenous vein, peroneus tertius, peroneus longus/brevis, physis, and fibula are encountered.

structures_at_risk.text: Superficial peroneal and sural nerves, short saphenous vein, peroneal tendons, distal-fibular physis/perichondral ring, fragment periosteum, and ankle cartilage are at risk.

danger_zones.text: Identify the superficial peroneal nerve proximally and sural nerve posteriorly before extending; minimize stripping around physis and fragment.

retraction_hazards.text: Use broad atraumatic retraction and avoid sustained pressure on sensory nerves or peroneal tendons.

exposure.text: Provides direct access to distal fibular shaft and lateral malleolar fragment with plate offset from incision.

limitations.text: Does not expose distal-tibial articular fragments and aggressive circumferential dissection threatens bone blood supply and physis.

extensions.text: Extend proximally or distally only after identifying the sensory nerve at risk and preserving tendon and physeal tissues.

indications.text: Use for displaced pediatric distal-fibular/lateral-malleolar fractures requiring open reduction, direct physeal alignment, or plate fixation.

relative_contraindications.text: Avoid open exposure for stable nondisplaced low-risk injuries and choose a posterior corridor when dominant posterior tibial pathology requires it.

implant_implications.text: Offset the plate from skin incision, respect physis and joint, and avoid screw trajectories that injure peroneal tendons or cross growth plate unnecessarily.

fluoroscopy_implications.text: Confirm length, rotation, mortise congruity, physeal alignment, and extra-articular implant position on AP, lateral, mortise, and oblique views.

closure.text: Restore peroneal fascia without nerve or tendon entrapment, confirm hemostasis, and close subcutaneous tissue and skin separately without plate prominence.

complications.text: Complications include physeal arrest, angular deformity, superficial-peroneal or sural neuropathy, tendon irritation, wound breakdown, infection, symptomatic hardware, and stiffness.

bailouts.text: Add a separate distal-tibial fragment-directed approach rather than circumferentially extending the fibular exposure across ankle.

procedure_applications.condition: A displaced distal-fibular or lateral-malleolar fracture requires direct reduction and fixation

questions.question: What is the deep interval?
questions.answer: Between peroneus tertius anteriorly and peroneus longus/brevis posteriorly.

questions.question: Why bias incision posteriorly?
questions.answer: So a lateral plate does not lie directly beneath incision.

questions.question: Which nerves bound proximal and posterior extension?
questions.answer: Superficial peroneal nerve proximally/anteriorly and sural nerve posteriorly.
